headline: Growth accelerates, margins expand, buybacks begin
summary_short: Duolingo's Q1 2026 revenue rose 27% y/y to $292M on subscriber and advertising growth, gross margin expanded to 73.0% from 71.1%, and net income rose 24% y/y to $43.5M; the company also began repurchasing shares under a new $400M buyback authorization.
summary_long: Revenue grew 27% y/y to $292.0M, driven by 31% growth in subscription revenue (more paid subscribers, higher ARPU) and 3% growth in advertising/other revenue. Gross margin expanded to 73.0% from 71.1% on lower per-unit AI costs and feature efficiency, partly offset by higher hosting costs. R&D rose 18% on headcount and AI/software costs; sales & marketing rose 47% on direct-marketing spend; G&A rose 7% on facilities costs. Net income rose to $43.5M (+24% y/y) on revenue growth and margin expansion; Adjusted EBITDA rose to $83.4M. Operating cash flow rose 43% y/y to $150.8M. In February 2026 the board authorized a $400M buyback program; $25.8M of shares were repurchased in the quarter. No forward guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Company attributed the quarter's growth to continued expansion in paid subscribers and average revenue per user, plus advertising growth from higher DAUs and price per ad served.

Subscription revenue rose 31% on growth in average paid subscribers and, to a lesser extent, higher average revenue per user; other revenue rose 3% on higher advertising revenue from more DAUs and price per ad.
Gross margin expanded to 73.0% from 71.1% on continued reductions in per-unit AI costs and improved feature efficiency (including Video Call), partly offset by higher hosting costs.
Company attributed the $8.3M net income increase to 27% revenue growth combined with a 30% gross-profit increase reflecting margin expansion and operating leverage.
Diluted EPS rose 23.6% y/y roughly in line with the 23.7% rise in net income, since weighted diluted shares outstanding grew only 1.0% y/y.
Increase was primarily driven by higher operating income and changes in working capital.
